# Dimorphos’s Orbit Continued to Change After DART

Dimorphos orbits the larger asteroid Didymos. Before DART’s impact, its orbital period was 11 hours and 55 minutes.

Immediately after the impact, Dimorphos’s period was shorter. It continued to shorten over the following weeks, during which Dimorphos also lost more rocky material to space.

The period eventually settled at about 11 hours and 22 minutes—roughly 33 minutes shorter than before the impact. Dimorphos’s orbit was also no longer circular.
